objective: Synchronize installation, user, model, roadmap, and status documentation with the published v1.0.1 package, the frozen v0.2.0 scientific baseline, and the latest verified independent DR24 recovery evidence. Preserve all scientific limitations and fail-closed acceptance criteria.
previous_knowledge_consumed: Official IRSA DR24 HATS documentation states that ZTF object identifiers are defined per filter, field, and quadrant; multiple OIDs are not automatically false positives.
The official BTS explorer snapshot retrieved on 2026-11-02 contains 10,551 rows and is preserved with SHA-256 af2362275074ff4b6c70523b9db6f2d5991af16fdd8d76ed47520948eb788e82.
Initial 100-object BTS-to-DR24 pilot run 41488299913 returned 773 OID rows within 5 arcseconds and showed strong radius-dependent multiplicity.
The existing StarEmbed adapter requires a verified Hugging Face revision and five Parquet artifacts; its coordinate-recovery pilot remains separate and pending.
Schema-aware BTS-to-DR24 source-backed run 41525750067 completed 100 targets and 773 unique OIDs; the live Objects Table schema exposed field, ccdid, qid, and fid.
The DR24 Lightcurves HATS table uses an objectid index; Objects Table presence does not prove a light-curve row exists.
Issue #188 raw DR24 light-curve artifact shows OIDs are single-filter: 5/12 selected OIDs were zi-only; the other 7 produced single-band, 19/42-finite feature vectors.

root_causes: The previous installation/user documentation did not consistently distinguish the published Python package from planned self-contained desktop installers.
The status report's source-backed Lightcurves availability check was stale because the final artifact had not yet been inspected when the first report draft was written.
The documentation-only PR failed the cumulative lifecycle gate because the workflow requires a cycle record for meaningful documentation changes.
unresolved: Complete and inspect runtime smoke, package build, and dependency audit for PR #247 after the lifecycle record was added.
Synchronize the main handbook and remaining operational acceptance documentation.
Do not claim scientific validation from documentation or contract checks.

findings: The v1.0.1 release is a Python package, not a self-contained desktop installer.
The frozen v0.2.0 scientific baseline and v1.0.1 software release are separate version identities and must be stated separately.
A successful indexed Lightcurves lookup proves row availability only; it does not prove clean photometry, sufficient cadence, source identity, or model readiness.
The 100-target BTS→DR24 pilot found 714 Lightcurves rows for 773 recovered OIDs; 59 OIDs had no row. These counts are bounded sample evidence only.
A weighted platform readiness estimate is an engineering planning measure, not a scientific validation metric.

open_blockers: Documentation changes do not implement astrophysical source grouping or g/r feature-engine integration.
Photometry quality, cadence, source identity, StarEmbed leakage, desktop packaging, and full product scientific acceptance remain open.

knowledge_carried_forward: Keep software release v1.0.1 distinct from frozen scientific baseline v0.2.0 / baseline_v0.2.
Do not call a Python wheel a self-contained desktop installer.
Use source-backed DR24 availability counts with their sample size, manifest, hashes, and limitations.
Do not treat Lightcurves row availability as proof of scientific usability.
Do not change scientific baselines or acceptance criteria to improve readiness scores.
